previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old woman with a history of coronary artery disease, diabetes, hypertension, and migraines was admitted for abdominal pain, headache, nausea, vomiting, and chest pressure. She had elevated blood pressure and blood glucose on presentation. Evaluation ruled out acute cardiac ischemia with normal ECGs and negative troponins. A CT scan revealed significant fecal loading, explaining her abdominal symptoms. Her headache, consistent with her migraine history, improved with acetaminophen and blood pressure control. Hyponatremia was corrected with IV fluids. Constipation was treated with senna, bisacodyl, and continued docusate, leading to bowel movements overnight. Her Lantus insulin dose was increased to 50 units due to persistent hyperglycemia. She engaged with social work regarding unsafe housing conditions. She was discharged home in stable condition with medication adjustments and follow-up plans.

Brief Hospital Course:
# Abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting: Patient asymptomatic on 
arrival to the floor, appears to be improved after GI cocktail 
in ED. LFTs benign, except for a chronic mild alkaline 
phosphatase elevation without tbili elevation, which improved on 
repeat labs. Patient stated similar to reflux symptoms and 
improved after GI cocktail. With unchanged EKG and CE x 2 neg 
unlikely cardiac. UA negative so UTI unlikely. Patient had large 
bowel movement x2 with laxatives and stool softeners with 
resolution of her abdominal pain.  She was discharged on her 
home bowel regimen and also with a new prescription for 
ranitidine and was instructed to follow up with her pcp ___ 
___ days of discharge.

# Chest pain: Given unchanged EKG, CE x 2 neg, unlikely to be 
cardiac, especially since the pt was ___ 1 month ago for the 
same complaint.  No radiation, diaphoresis or dyspnea. Likely GI 
related given the simultaneous nausea and vomiting.  She was 
discharged on her home BB, ASA, ACEI and statin.  A message was 
left with her pcp's office regarding her hospital stay, and she 
was instructed to follow up with him to schedule an outpatient 
stress test.

# Acute Renal Failure: Cr 1.2 up from baseline of 0.9. BUN 
elevation, mild lactate elevation consistent with prerenal 
(hypotension) in the setting of vomiting and poor po intake 
prior to admission.  She received IV fluids overnight and her 
Cre improved to 1.0.

# Diabetes Mellitus - Hyperglycemic on arrival to floor, likely 
in setting of acute stress. No anion gap.  She was continued on 
her evening lantus regimen with 17units novolin with meals as 
well as an insulin sliding scale.     
.  
# Hypertension - ACEI and HCTZ were held overnight in the 
setting of her acute renal failure; she was instructed to 
continue these medications on discharge.   
.  
# Hyperlipidemia - Continued statin.  
.  
# Migraine - Consistent with usual episodes, improved by the 
time she arrived to the floor.  She was written for tylenol prn 
and required one dose the morning of discharge.  
.
# Social - The patient complained of cockroach infestation at 
her apartment and was concerned about returning home.  She was 
informed that unfortunately this is not an indication for 
continued hospitalization, but social work was consulted and 
advised of the situation in case the Department of Health needed 
notification.
